Data rather than code so the mapping is readable, diffable, and assertable from a CJS test — jest's node project cannot import an .mjs.
//noTestsNeeded: Paths that derive NO tests BY DESIGN, each with the reason. This is the
third category, and it exists because the empty-population refusal would
otherwise block a README edit: 'no rule covers this' and 'no test could
cover this' are different answers and only one of them is a problem.
Shrink-only in spirit — an entry here is a claim that nothing in the

noTestsNeeded.why: Top-level prose for humans. No guard reads them; CLAUDE.md is the exception and has its own rule because guards quote it.
Tooling config with no test surface. `generated-artifacts-have-no-merge-driver` asserts .gitattributes has no merge driver, and that guard is reached by the content rule on the driver syntax itself.
Editor-local settings; nothing in the repo reads them.

pathRules.why: A change under tests/ puts META-guards in scope — ones that grade the SHAPE of test code (hand-rolled file walks, comment strippers, guard-file ceilings) rather than the code under test. Measured twice: `file-collection-is-not-silently-empty` fired on a helper inside a new test, and its subject ("which guards exist") has nothing to do with any change topic.
Route coverage, the route inventory and the OpenAPI completeness contracts all range over the route tree, and none of them live beside the route.
The i18n gate checks bg/en key parity, orphans, drift and untranslated values across the whole catalogue, so one added key is a whole-catalogue question.
The generated spec is committed, so a path edit without `npm run openapi:generate` leaves it stale, and the contract snapshots pin its prose.
Schema-folder coverage, destructive-migration inverses and RLS guards are all derived from the schema rather than from the migration you wrote.

docs/ is NOT test-free, which is what I assumed when I first declared it so. Derived: 64 distinct docs files are read by tests, and the sweeps make it worse than a list suggests — no-legacy-brand scans docs for the previous brand name, so ANY file here can fail a guard, and vm-runbook-commands asserts every repo path docs/runbooks/production-vm.md names still exists. Even docs/implementation-notes/ is read by five guards. Found by editing the runbook and watching verify:changed report `none with a test surface` for a file its own guardrail reads.

Six guards read infra/: oi-3-alerting and oi-3-runbook-and-slos assert the declared alert policies and SLO targets, infra-directories-are-referenced fails when a directory here is referenced by nothing, and the restore-drill pair (shell-heredoc-no-live-backticks, restore-drill-remote-script) pins the quoted heredoc whose un-quoting left the drill dead for a month.

public/ is not static assets only. public/sw.js is the outbox's PARALLEL reimplementation — it cannot import from src/, so its copy is mirrored BY HAND and outbox-completion-mirrors-the-sw exists to enforce that mirror; eight test files across three roots read it (also sw-revision-stamp, sw-offline-route-integrity, web-push, the two registrar suites). public/fonts is pinned by vendored-font-integrity and font-preload-derived-from-lock. Before this rule a change to the service worker derived NOTHING.

Covers dependabot.yml too (dependabot-typescript-eslint-group and typescript-eslint-family-is-coherent both read it), not just workflows and scripts. Several guards assert against .github itself rather than against src: ci-failure-watchlist DERIVES the notifier's watch list from the workflow files, ci-aggregate-upstream-failure lifts each aggregate's run: block out of ci.yml and executes it, shell-heredoc-no-live-backticks pins the restore drill's quoted delimiter, and restore-drill-remote-script compares the payload byte-for-byte. Added because a 2026-10-25 change to three .github files derived ZERO paths and so ran the entire suite: the watchlist guard had to be run by hand to discover it was demanding the new workflow.

Compose/image guards assert drift against the repo-canonical files and the env template. tests/unit/deploy holds the EXECUTING tests for the deploy scripts — compare-running-state.py's exit codes, prune-backups.sh, verify-image-deps.mjs — which a structural guard cannot cover, since what matters there is what the script DOES. Those three suites sat outside this rule: #2288 created that root and did not add the line, so a change to the comparator never ran the suite written for it.
Dependency ratchets and the lockfile guards. A lockfile written by the wrong npm also drops platform `libc` constraints, which only a guard notices.
Rendered tests, the design-system drift guardrail and the public-surface guards all range over components rather than over the file you edited.
The default population for source changes. Broad on purpose: it is the root that held the failing assertion in the first of the three wrong subsets this issue records.
Several guards quote CLAUDE.md or assert that a claim in it is true, so editing it can fail a test with no code change at all.

contentRules.why: A NEW refusal code needs a Bulgarian entry and a name in the OpenAPI spec. Both guards live far from the throwing file, and both fired on #2035 after everything else was green.
A new path that stores uploaded bytes joins two derived populations — the metadata strippers and the past-due upload gate. #2030: four paths had escaped the second one.
Changing how an uploaded FORMAT is treated puts every suite holding a fixture of that format in scope. On #2035 that was 47 suites, 35 outside the import-derived set.
The lint ceiling counts SUPPRESSED findings, so a new disable can redden CI with no new warning. Re-run the ceiling AFTER the last edit — a stale run is one of the three failures this issue records.
The capability ruling and its gate coverage are checked by a derived population, not by the file holding the gate.
